maya: FYI perf alert: observed KV page-eviction thrash for model/gpt-large routes during a sustained long-context workload. Latency tail jumped ~120ms p99.
perf-bot: ALERT: kv-residency > 85% on node gpu-03 for 15m; eviction-rate spike. Chart: http://grafana/redwood/d/kv/kv-residency (auto) :warning:
maya: copying logs & a short snippet of the eviction-rate timeline:
```
2026-03-17T21:03:12Z node=gpu-03 eviction_rate=123 req/s kv_residency=87% p99_latency=470ms
2026-03-17T21:03:42Z node=gpu-03 eviction_rate=210 req/s kv_residency=90% p99_latency=590ms
```
jon: Received. I pulled a flamegraph from the reproducer. Initial look points to repeated prefix misses that then re-load full pages. Attaching stack snippet from `perf script`:
```
kv_page_load() -> deserialize_kv_page() -> apply_prefix() -> model_forward()
```
liam: :thinking_face: Are we sure it's misses and not fragmentation? Our key scheme uses `tenant + model + prefix + session_id` salt — if session churn is high, keys won't coalesce and pages will fill with near-identical prefixes.
anya: Replayed a 30m trace with KV debug headers. Same behavior: same logical prefix is getting re-created every request because client session_id changes frequently (ephemeral session tokens). Reuse rate for that prefix dropped from ~78% to ~24% across the trace.
maya: Sounds like classic page thrash: hotset larger than page_capacity, combined with churned keys. Current eviction is plain LRU at page granularity which amplifies churn. Two levers: increase page size or change eviction/admission (e.g., seglist / TinyLFU). Also consider canonicalizing keys so session-unique parts don't create distinct entries.
jon: Proposed experiment plan:
1) Implement prefix canonicalization (strip session-like suffixes) behind a config flag
2) Add a route-level hint header to opt-in pins (e.g., `x-kv-reuse-hint: window=10`) so app can say requests are sticky
3) Try TinyLFU-style admission with a small freq table to avoid one-offs filling pages.
liam: Quick note: current keying code is `sha256(tenant || ':' || model || ':' || prefix || ':' || session_id)` in `runtime_keying.rs`. Minimal change: produce normalized_prefix = normalize(prefix) then `sha256(tenant || ':' || model || ':' || normalized_prefix)` — low-risk patch but must be opt-in per tenant.
anya: Normalization looks effective in the replay, but caution: normalizing might accidentally allow cross-session cache access if prefix contains ephemeral or PII tokens. We need an allowlist/denylist approach and opt-in by tenant/route.
maya: Agreed. Default to disabled. Add config: `kv.reuse.normalization.enabled=false` with per-route override. Also add a metric `kv.reuse.normalized_hits_total` and `kv.eviction_rate` to monitor.
perf-bot: Canary: rolling out to 2 nodes with `kv.reuse.normalization=true` for model/gpt-large routes. Monitor p95/p99, eviction-rate, and a new `kv.reuse.by_prefix_v2` histogram.
jon: Early canary numbers (~10m in): eviction_rate decreased ~40% on canary nodes, p99 tail down ~70ms. Interesting side-effect: token-throughput increased because more cache hits, which bumped CPU on the kernel-selection path (more deserialization & kernel dispatches).
liam: That CPU bump matches what I saw locally. More hits -> more KV deserialization hot-path work. We should consider moving KV page de-serialization off the request-critical path into a pooled worker or use a zero-copy mapper for frequently hit pages.
anya: I'll open a follow-up PR for pooled buffers + zero-copy mapping for read-only page access, and include tests to ensure normalization can't leak sensitive tokens. Will make normalization opt-in per tenant and add route docs.
maya: Thanks. Keep the canary run for at least 12h. If anything regresses, we'll rollback the normalization flag. /cc @oncall
perf-bot: NOTE: Canary healthy at 15m, metrics: eviction_rate=35% (down), kv_residency=63%, p99=420ms (was 490ms). Continuing monitoring. :eyes:
jon: Also adding a microbenchmark to test combined effect of normalization + TinyLFU admission + pooled deserialization in isolation. Will post results here when ready.
liam: FYI patch location: `runtime/keying/runtime_keying.rs` + `runtime/kv/eviction.rs` for TinyLFU prototype.
anya: I'll handle docs + config schema change.
maya: Great work team. Leaving this thread open until canary completes. If we see any kernel-selection perf regressions, raise a separate thread to triage batching/kernel heuristics.
